name: sqlite_freespace
description: Text fragments from the free space of a SQLite database's MAIN file: freelist pages, the unallocated gap of each b-tree page and the freeblock chain of freed cells. A fragment is text, not a row: no column, no table, no time, no row boundary, and the page may have belonged to something else. SENSITIVE: free pages of a messenger database hold message text and sometimes credentials, so the answer carries where each fragment is (finding_id, page, kind of region, byte offset, length in bytes and characters, encoding) and never its text; the text is written only on write_values: true, in a job run with secret_output: true, to $OUT/sqlite-freespace-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created before the scan, refused if it exists; the request is refused outside a job). Every offset is the byte position in the file and was read back from the file and compared before it was reported (offset_verified). Encodings: UTF-8 (any language) and UTF-16LE (Latin including Latin Additional, Greek including Greek Extended, Cyrillic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, Arabic, Devanagari, Thai and common punctuation; CJK, kana, Hangul and emoji only in runs of at least 8 characters, a lower-confidence reading; other scripts are not found), read at either byte parity, and UTF-16BE instead of UTF-16LE where the header declares UTF-16BE; text in another encoding, in a binary column or compressed or encrypted is not found, so a negative covers only those encodings and only the regions counted under scanned. A -wal, -shm or -journal beside the file is listed with its size and NOT examined: committed changes that only the WAL holds are absent, and a rollback journal's page images are not read; a -wal or -journal that holds bytes makes the status partial. The header is validated (page size, usable size, format versions, declared size against the file); the freelist is walked with a cycle check and compared with the header's count; every freeblock chain is checked for order, bounds and loops; lock-byte and pointer-map pages are skipped and counted. status is complete, partial (a time limit, a companion not read, pages not examined) or corrupt (the structure disagreed with itself where problems says; fragments found are still reported). A file that is not SQLite is refused with its size and, if it has 256 bytes or more, the entropy of its first 4 KiB, never its first bytes. contains narrows the sealed values file and nothing else: it needs write_values: true in a job run with secret_output: true (otherwise it is refused before anything is scanned), and the answer lists every fragment whatever the expression matched and does not say how many matched, since a list of the matches would tell, fragment by fragment, whether text you cannot see matches it. It runs on text nobody can see, so how long it takes must not tell anything about that text either: only an expression of bounded cost is accepted (literals, classes, anchors, groups, alternation, and repeats with an upper bound of one piece that holds no choice; no *, + or {m,}, no nested repeat, no lookahead or lookbehind, no back reference, at most 256 characters, at most 16384 in worst-case steps), and a fragment on which it still runs out of time is written to the values file as if it had matched, with no count, no problem and no change to the pages read. A job whose arguments include write_values is run as secret output (the manifest declares it), and the tool refuses write_values in a job that is not. Whole results are kept: the inline page is limit rows and the rest is in the file the answer names. Not a deleted-record reconstruction, not a WAL or journal reader, and not a statement that a database was or was not vacuumed.

db.description: A SQLite database file (the main file; its -wal and -journal are listed, not read)

min_length.description: Shortest run of text, in characters (default 6, at least 3)

contains.description: Case-insensitive regex over a fragment's text; it decides which fragments' text is written to the values file (the answer lists all of them, and does not say which matched). Needs write_values: true, in a job run with secret_output: true. Only an expression of bounded cost is accepted: at most 256 characters, repeats only with an upper bound ({m,n} or ?, not *, + or {m,}) and only of a piece that holds no choice, no lookahead, lookbehind or back reference, and a worst case of at most 16384 steps. A fragment on which it runs out of time is written as if it had matched and nothing reports it

limit.description: Fragments in the inline answer (default 200, and at most 1 MiB of rows); the whole list is in the file the answer names

write_values.description: Write each reported fragment's text to $OUT/sqlite-freespace-values.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the answer never carries a text

max_seconds.description: Stop before the next page after this long (default 240, at most 270); the pages not reached are counted and the answer says partial
